newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria railway raises tariffs to win funding.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria railway raises tariffs to win funding.

text.p: Bulgaria's state railway will raise passenger tariffs by 58 percent from April 20 to meet a requirement of the International Monetary Fund and win a loan of up to $20 million, BSR general director said on Wednesday.

Yordan Mirchev said an accord signed last month by the IMF and the Bulgarian interim government to stabilise the country's shattered economy, had included funding the railway if its revenue covers half of the expenditure.
"We raised freight rates by 250 percent on April 1 and after increasing the passanger tariffs we will meet the IMF requirement," Mirchev told a news conference.
He said that as a result of price hikes the railway would achieve a daily income of one billion levs and its income in April would total 22-23 billion levs.
The debt-ridden railway has borrowed $152 million from international lending institutions to carry out a restructuring programme and a programme for its financial stabilisation.
The new management of the railway plans to attract potential foreign investors through the establishment of joint ventures as only one venture had been set up so far, Mirchev said.
A joint venture between Austria's engineering firm VAE Eisenbahnsystems AG and a Sofia railway point plant has been set up and its first general meeting will be in May, Mirchev said.
Another joint venture would be set up with a plant producing sleepers for railway tracks and electric pylons in the Danube River port of Svistov, he added.

The railway plans to spend $23.8 million from its $45 million loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), extended for the company's restructuring programme, for wagon refurbishment.

Mirchev said the company would invite bidders for the completion of its section of a railway link with Macedonia, which is part of an East-West route from the Bulgarian Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas via Macedonia to Duras in Albania.
He did not specify when the tender would be announced.
